pp:me:2024:q1.question:
In order to numerically solve the ordinary differential equation $\frac{d y}{d t}=-y$ for $t > 0$, with an initial condition $y(0)=1$, the following scheme is employed

$\frac{\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{n}+1}-\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{n}}}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=-\frac{1}{2}\left(\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{n}-1}+\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{n}}\right)$

Here, $\Delta t$ is the time step and $y_{n}=y(n \Delta t)$ for $n$ $=0,1,2, \ldots$ Thus numerical scheme will yield a solution with non-physical oscillations for $\Delta \mathrm{t} > \mathrm{h}$. The value of $\mathrm{h}$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given,

$$\begin{aligned}

\frac{y_{n+1}-y_n}{\Delta t} & =\frac{1}{2}\left(y_{n+1}+y_n\right) \\

y_{n+1}-y_n & =\frac{\Delta t}{2}\left(y_{n+1}+y_n\right) \\

y_{n+1}-\frac{\Delta t}{2} y_{n+1} & =y_n+\frac{\Delta t}{2} y_n \\

y_{n+1} & =\frac{2+\Delta t}{2-\Delta t} y_n

\end{aligned}$$

For stability or non physical oscillations,

$$\begin{aligned}

\left|\frac{2+\Delta t}{2-\Delta t}\right| & \leq 1 \\

-1 & \leq \frac{2+\Delta t}{2-\Delta t} \leq 1 \\

-1 & \leq-1+\frac{4}{2-\Delta t} \leq 1 \\

0 & \leq \frac{4}{2-\Delta t} \leq 2 \\

\frac{1}{2} & \leq \frac{2-\Delta t}{4} \leq 0 \\

2 & \leq 2-\Delta t \leq 0 \\

0 & \leq-\Delta t \leq-2 \\

\Delta t & \geq 2

\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore \quad \Delta t \geq 2$

pp:me:2024:q3.title: GATE ME 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 3
pp:me:2024:q3.question: Let $f(z)$ be an analytic function, where $z=x+i y$. If the real part of $f(z)$ is $\cosh x \cos y$, and the imaginary part of $f(z)$ is zero for $y=0$, then $f(z)$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
The necessary and sufficient condition for a function $f(z)=u(x, y)+i v(x, y)$ to be analytic is it should satisfy the cauchy Riemann equation.

C.R. equation:

$\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y} \quad \text { or, } \quad u_{x}=v_{y}$

$\&, \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}$ or, $u_{y}=-v_{x}$

Given: $\quad \mathrm{u}=\cosh \mathrm{x} \cos y$

Now, $\quad u_{x}=\sinh x \cos y$

and, $\quad u_{y}=-\cosh x \sin y$

To find $f(z)$, put $x=z \& y=0$;

$$\begin{aligned}

f(z)&=\int\left(u_{x}-i u_{y}\right) d z \\

&=\int[\sinh z \cdot \cos 0-(-\cosh z \cdot \sin 0)] d z \\

&=\int \sinh z d z=\cosh z+C

\end{aligned}$$

The velocity field of a two-dimensional, incompressible flow is given by

$\vec{V}=2 \sinh x \hat{i}+v(x, y) \hat{j}$

where $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ denote the unit vectors in $x$ and $y$ directions, respectively. If $v(x, 0)=\cosh x$, then $v(0,-1)$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:

Given; the velocity field of a two-dimensional, incompressible flow,

$\vec{V}=2 \sinh x \hat{i}+v(x, y) \hat{j} \& \quad v(x, 0)=\cosh x$

Now, $\nabla \cdot \vec{V}=0$ (for an incompressible flow)

i.e. $\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}=0$

$2 \cosh x+\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}=0$

$\Rightarrow \quad \partial \mathbf{v}=-2 \cosh \mathrm{x} \cdot \partial \mathrm{y}$

Integrate both sides,

$$\begin{aligned}

& \int \partial v=-\int 2 \cosh x \cdot \partial y \\

& v=-2 y \cosh x+C  \;\;\;...(1)

\end{aligned}$$

Given; $\mathrm{v}(\mathrm{x}, 0)=\cosh \mathrm{x}$

$\therefore \quad \cosh x=-2(0) \cosh x+C$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{C}=\cosh \mathrm{x}$

Now, from equation (1)

$$\begin{aligned}

v(x, y) & =-2 y \cosh x+\cosh x \\

& =(1-2 y) \cosh x

\end{aligned}$$

At $(0,-1)$

$$\begin{aligned}

\mathrm{v}(0,-1) & =[1-2(-1)] \cosh (0) \\

& =3

\end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2024:q21.title: GATE ME 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 21
pp:me:2024:q21.question: The allowance provided to a pattern for easy withdrawal from a sand mold is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Types of allowances:

Draft/taper allowances.

Machining allowance/finishing allowance.

Distortion allowances/camber allowance

Shrinkage allowance/contraction allowances.

Shake allowance/rapping allowance.

Shake allowance

Before withdrawal from the sand mould, the pattern is wrapped all around the vertical faces to enlarge the mould cavity slightly, which facilitates its removal. Since it enlarge the final casting made, it is desirable that the original pattern dimensions should be reduced to account for this increase. There is no sure way of quantifying this allowance, since it is highly dependent on the foundry personnel and practices involved.

It is negative allowance and is to be applied only to those dimensions, which are parallel to the parting plane. One way of reducing this allowance is to increase the draft, which can be removed during the subsequent matching.

Draft/taper allowances

Once pattern is embedded in the moulding sand now it is required to withdrawing the pattern from moulding sand, for this propose a vertical force is required to lift the pattern. For easy removal of pattern from mould cavity there should be some degree or $\mathrm{mm}$ taper in the pattern.

If there is no taper in the pattern then more chance to break the mould cavity wall during withdrawing the pattern. Draft allowance varies with the complexity of job.

Machining or Finishing allowance

In sand casting operation machining/finishing allowances is given in the pattern as on solidification every metal get shrinked up to some extend and the outer surface of object (casting) is rough, therefore, to smoothing the outer surface of casting machining allowance is must.

Distortion allowance/Camber allowance

On just solidification of metal casting is weak, therefore, more chances to distorted casting. Chance of distortion are basically in $U, V$, then long section or complicated casting. Distortion can be minimized or eliminated by providing an allowance and constructed the pattern initially distorted, i.e. opposite in outer side direction. Among of distortion allowance varies from 1.5$20 \mathrm{~mm}$.

It is the tendency of all metals that they shrink after cooling except bismuth, Shrinkage is only due to inter atomic vibration which are implified by increasing in temperature. Metal shrink or contract in three ways :

Liquid Contraction

Solidification Contraction

Solid Contraction

pp:me:2024:q50.title: GATE ME 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 50
pp:me:2024:q50.question: A cutting tool provides a tool life of 60 minutes while machining with the cutting speed of $60 \mathrm{~m} /$ $\mathrm{min}$. When the same tool is used for machining the same material, it provides a tool life of 10 minutes for a cutting speed of $100 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{min}$. If the cutting speed is changed to $80 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{min}$ for the same tool and work material combination, the tool life computed using Taylor's tool life model is _____ minutes (rounded off to 2 decimal places).

detailed_solution.concept: Manufacturing Engineering - Machining and Machine Tool Operation
detailed_solution.markdown:
Taylor Tool Life Equation

$$\begin{aligned}

\mathrm{VT}^{\mathrm{n}} & =\text { Constant } \\

\mathrm{V}_{1} \mathrm{~T}_{1}^{\mathrm{n}} & =\mathrm{V}_{2} \mathrm{~T}_{2}^{\mathrm{n}}=\mathrm{V}_{3} \mathrm{~T}_{3}^{\mathrm{n}} \\

\mathrm{V}_{1} \mathrm{~T}_{1}^{\mathrm{n}} & =\mathrm{V}_{2} \mathrm{~T}_{2}^{\mathrm{n}}

\end{aligned}$$

Given : $V_{1}=60 \frac{\mathrm{m}}{\min }, T_{1}=60 \mathrm{~min}$

$\mathrm{V}_{2}=100 \frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{min}}, \mathrm{T}_{2}=10 \mathrm{~min}$

So, to find out $n, V_{1} T_{1}^{n}=V_{2} T_{2}^{n}$

$$\begin{aligned}

\operatorname{InV_{1}+n\operatorname {nn}T_{1}} & =\ln \mathrm{V}_{2}+\mathrm{nlnT}_{2} \\

\ln \mathrm{V}_{1}-\operatorname{InV_{2}} & =\mathrm{n}\left[\ln \mathrm{T}_{2}-\operatorname{InT_{1}]}\right. \\

\mathrm{n} & =\frac{\ln \mathrm{V}_{1}-\ln \mathrm{V}_{2}}{\operatorname{lnT_{2}-\operatorname {ln}\mathrm {T}_{1}}} \\

& =\frac{\ln (60)-\ln (100)}{\ln (10)-\ln (60)}=0.285

\end{aligned}$$

Now, $\mathrm{V}_{3}=80 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{min}, \mathrm{T}_{3}=$ ?

$\mathrm{V}_{3} \mathrm{~T}_{3}^{\mathrm{n}}=\mathrm{V}_{2} \mathrm{~T}_{2}^{\mathrm{n}}$

$$\begin{aligned}

\text { So, } & 80 \times \mathrm{T}_{3}^{0.285} & =100 \times 10^{0.285} \\

\Rightarrow & \mathrm{T}_{3} & =21.87 \mathrm{~min}

\end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2024:q59.question:
The real variable $x, y, z$ and the real constants $p, q, r$ satisfy.

$\frac{x}{p q-r^{2}}=\frac{y}{q r-p^{2}}=\frac{z}{r p-q^{2}}$

Given that the denominators are non-zero, the value of $p x+q y+r z$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned}

& \text { Let } \frac{x}{p q-r^{2}}=\frac{y}{q r-p^{2}}=\frac{2}{r p-q^{2}}=K \\

& \Rightarrow \quad x=K\left(p q-r^{2}\right) \\

& \qquad \begin{array}{l}

y=K\left(q r-p^{2}\right) \\

z=K\left(r p-q^{2}\right)

\end{array}

\end{aligned}$$

So, $p x+q y+r z=$

$K \times p\left(p q-r^{2}\right)+K \times q\left(q r-p^{2}\right)+K \times r\left(r p-q^{2}\right)$

$=K\left(p^{2} q-p r^{2}+q^{2} r-q p^{2}+r^{2} p-r q^{2}\right)$

$=\mathrm{K} \times 0=0$
